@@ -74438,6 +74440,148 @@ body { display:none } checkers. A user agent could offer on-demand checking, could perform continuous checking while the checking is enabled, or could use other interfaces.

+

Autocapitalization

+ +

Some methods of entering text, for example voice input and on-screen keyboards on mobile + devices, assist users by automatically capitalizing the first letter of sentences (when composing + text in a language with this convention). The + autocapitalize attribute allows authors to override such + behavior. The autocapitalize attribute, as typically + implemented, does not affect behavior when typing on a physical keyboard.

+ +

The autocapitalize attribute can be used on an editing host to control autocapitalization behavior for the hosted + editable region, on an input or textarea element to control the behavior + for inputting text into that element, or on a form element to control the default + behavior for child input and textarea elements. + +

The autocapitalize attribute never causes + autocapitalization to be enabled for input elements whose type attribute is in one of the URL, E-mail, or Password states (this behavior is included in the + used autocapitalization hint algorithm below). + +

The autocapitalize attribute is an + enumerated attribute whose keywords are on, off, none, sentences, words, and characters.

+ +

The keywords off and none map to the none + state. The keyword words maps to the words state and the keyword + characters maps to the characters state. The keywords on and sentences map to the sentences state, + which is also the invalid value default. The missing value default is a separate default state.
body: I would prefer we make a table from the above two paragraphs and also included a brief description. See https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-button-type for precedent. That way the meaning of the values are also somewhat clear in the developer's edition.
